heading: INT. HOTEL ASTORIA SWITCHBOARD ROOM - NIGHT (1927)

units.text: INT. HOTEL ASTORIA SWITCHBOARD ROOM - NIGHT (1927)
A narrow room behind the lobby.
A tall brass switchboard glows with a hundred tiny bulbs.
A desk lamp, a half-eaten sandwich, a cup of cocoa going cold.
ADELAIDE PRUITT-ROSS, 20s, a headset over her marcelled waves, plugs a cable into a jack with practiced calm.
She hums.
A BELLHOP named FLOYD, 17, lingers in the doorway, hat in hand, watching her.
Miss Adelaide, the gentleman in 412 wants his bags brought up and his brandy brought down.
units.name: FLOYD

units.text: That's the wrong way round.
units.name: ADELAIDE

units.text: That's what he said.
units.name: FLOYD

units.text: Then he's had too much brandy.
units.name: ADELAIDE

units.text: She plugs another cable.
A bulb winks out.
Floyd steps into the room to see better, bumps the desk, and the cocoa cup slides to the edge.
Adelaide catches it without looking, and in the same motion her other hand flicks a switch.
A voice crackles on the line.
Operator? Operator, I'd like the front desk, please.
units.name: CLARENCE

units.text: One moment, sir. Connecting.
units.name: ADELAIDE

units.text: She presses a key.
The voice is cut off.
She waits a beat, then removes her headset and sets it on the desk.
Who was that?
units.name: FLOYD

units.text: Nobody. A man asking for the front desk.
units.name: ADELAIDE

units.text: Isn't that your job?
units.name: FLOYD

units.text: Tonight, it's my pleasure to be difficult.
units.name: ADELAIDE

units.text: She takes a bite of the sandwich.
Floyd stares.
Then the board lights up all at once, every bulb at once, a Christmas tree of demand.
Adelaide stands.
The headset is back on her head before she has finished chewing.
Hotel Astoria, how may I direct your call?
units.name: ADELAIDE

units.text: Miss, I am the man in 412 and I would like it noted that I have been cut off three times.
units.name: CLARENCE

units.text: Noted, sir.
units.name: ADELAIDE

units.text: She flips a second switch with her elbow.
A new voice cuts in, dry and tired.
Front desk. Mr. Holcomb speaking. Adelaide, is that man still complaining?
units.name: HOLCOMB

units.text: He is, Mr. Holcomb. Quite warmly.
units.name: ADELAIDE
